segments.text: Good morning, everyone. This briefing of the Development Budget Coordination Committee, or the DBCC, is hereby called to order. Please rise for the singing of the national anthem and please remain standing for the opening prayer to be led by Vice Chairperson Johanne Bautista of the TRABAHO Party-list.

segments.speaker: Rep. Johanne Monich G. Bautista
segments.text: Let us put ourselves in the presence of Almighty God. Ever-living God, we bow our heads before You today with hearts full of gratitude and profound responsibility as we begin our budget briefing. Grant us, Lord, the wisdom, discernment, and steadfast dedication needed to craft a national budget that truly serves the Filipino people, a budget that drives economic recovery, creates sustainable and decent livelihoods, and uplifts every worker, family, and community across our archipelago. Lord God of creation, we also place before Your loving protection the Filipino people, especially as our nation faces the trials of inclement weather and natural calamities. We ask for Your merciful mantle of safety and security to shield every community, home, and vulnerable family. Please grant strength and resilience to our frontline workers, local leaders, and disaster response teams, and guide our hands to allocate the resources necessary to protect, prepare, and deliver swift aid to those in need. May everything we discuss and decide today and in the next few weeks be guided by integrity, compassion, and unwavering commitment to public service and the common good. Amen.

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: Consistent with our mandate, we worry about inflation because it diminishes the purchasing power of Filipino families. Low inflation also supports sustainable growth. We are encouraged to report that

segments.speaker: BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr.
segments.text: because oil is also the source of much of our fertilizer

segments.text: to contain price pressures the bsp has responded by tightening monetary policy

segments.text: twice this year these were carefully calibrated moves to help slow down inflation

segments.text: anchor inflation expectations while recognizing the temporary weakness in growth

segments.text: to decide on the next policy action we look at all the evidence and we are prepared

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: So let me start with some brief overview of what is happening in the economy.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: What is the latest trend in terms of inflation? In 2025, we see here that lower food, particularly

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: rice and energy prices significantly eased the country's inflation. This continued in the first

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: two months of this year, 2026. However, the conflict in the Middle East since end February

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: 2026 drove global oil prices higher, and this translated to significant spillover

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: to domestic inflation. Inflation rose from 2.4%

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: in February of this year to a recent peak at 7.2% in April. However, since then, it has gradually

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: eased to 6.2% by July. However, that number, that inflation number, continued to be well

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: above the target of 3%. The moderation that we have seen since the period May to July

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: in inflation reflects lower global oil prices and improve food supply conditions.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: What was the response of the BSP?

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: As the Governor has mentioned, monetary policy shifted to a tightening stance with this rise in

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: inflation, and also the increase in the inflation outlook. The BSP decided to raise target policy rates,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: from 4.25% by 25 basis points each in April and June 2026.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This brings the policy rate to 4.75%.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This calibrated move by the BSP helps anchor inflation expectations

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and reduce what we call second round risks.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: At the same time, this measured policy action supports growth.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja

segments.text: Where do we see inflation going this year and next year in 2027?

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: The inflation outlook has deteriorated amid the challenging external environment

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and amid the faster than expected broadening of price pressure.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: We can see this.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: We can tell from what we call core inflation numbers.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Our analysis point to stronger second round effects

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and a wider pass-through of earlier supply shocks

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: to the different components of the consumption basket.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: In the monetary policy meeting last June,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: the BSP sees headline inflation averaging at 6.4% in 2026,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And both numbers are above the inflation target of 3%.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: However, by 2028, it is possible that inflation will be close to the target

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: at around 3.1%.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: The BSP sees upside inflation risk,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and this could emanate largely from the higher global oil prices

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and higher inflation expectations.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: If you look at private sector inflation forecasts,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: they could also see higher inflation in the near term.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: But this could revert to near the 3% level by 2028 or 2029.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Now going to the banking system,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: how is the banking system performing?

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: The banking system remains healthy.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: The Philippine banking system is supported by strong fundamentals.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Banks sustain growth in assets and deposits

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and continued profitability.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Capital and liquidity metrics remain well above international standards,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and non-performing loans are manageable and well provisioned.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Looking ahead, the banking system is well positioned

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: to support economic activity

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and financial stability.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: We also observed that more Filipinos

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: continue to participate in the formal financial system.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: The chart on the left shows that digital payments

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: reached almost 65% of retail transactions last year.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This surpasses the targets of 50% to 54%.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And our data shows even more.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: In the last few months,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: we have seen an increase in the number of payments

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: that have been made through digital payments.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This is due to increasing use of payments

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: through Instapay, Pesonet, and person-to-merchant QRPH.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This highlights the continued momentum

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: on the adoption of electronic payments channels in the country.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Equally important,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: the growing adoption of digital payments

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: also generates what are called network externalities.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Electronic payment channels increase

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: as more consumers, more merchants,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and more financial institutions participate

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: in this financial ecosystem.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: On the right side,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: we show the increasing number of basic deposit accounts,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and it has reached over 28 million as of March 2026,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: with 177 banks offering basic deposits.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This is one of the ways

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: that we at the BSP promote financial inclusion.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: We also welcome the decision of several banks

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: to reduce or waive interbank digital transaction fees.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This reduction or waiver of interbank digital transaction fees

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: makes it more affordable and accessible

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: for Filipino households and small businesses

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: to access the convenience of electronic fund transfers.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: We also thank our legislators

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: for the passage of the Anti-Financial Accounts Coming Act.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This is indeed an important legislation

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: to continue to improve the consumer protection

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: through stronger safeguards for fraud

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and faster complaint resolutions.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: At the external front,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: if you look at our external sector,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: it continues to protect our economy

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: from the effects of the volatile external conditions.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Right now, we have a balance of payments deficit

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: of about 1.2% of GDP.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This is for last year,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and the current account narrowed

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: due to strong exports and remittances.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: For 2026 and 2027,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: the current account deficit is projected to slightly widen,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and this is consistent with the experience

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: of many emerging market economies

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: pursuing investment-led growth.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: For the Philippines,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: the wider deficit primarily reflects strong demand

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: for capital goods and other productive imports

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: needed to support infrastructure development

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and expand productive activity.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: How is this deficit being supported right now?

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This highlights the importance

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: of structural foreign exchange inflows,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: the remittances, the revenues from BPO's,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and also the inflows from foreign direct investments.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: We are also maintaining enough buffers

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: in terms of international reserves.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: As of now, our international reserve stands

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: at almost $105 billion.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: That is as of end June 2026,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and it's equivalent to about seven months' worth

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: of imports of goods and services.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: So this is the general macroeconomic landscape

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: that we are working with at this time.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: And the key assumptions behind the proposed national budget

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: for fiscal year 2027

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: are shown in this particular slide.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: In terms of inflation,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: as mentioned earlier,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: our latest inflation forecast

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: points to still elevated inflation for 2026

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: before easing in 2027.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: For the national government budget purposes,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: we assume that headline inflation

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: to be around 4% to 5% for 2027.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Oil prices remain volatile and highly uncertain,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: largely dependent on geopolitical developments,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: particularly in the Middle East.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Markets right now are pointing to some decline

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: in the price of Dubai crude oil

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: to about the range of $70 to $90 per barrel

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: on average in 2027.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Exchange rate will be broadly stable

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: against the US dollar,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: reflecting external developments

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and also at the same time some domestic headwinds.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: On the interest rates,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: particularly domestic interest rates,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: the one-year T-bill rate will range around 5% to 6%

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and this reflects the country's fiscal condition

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and the policy of continued consolidation.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: In the international interest rates,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: the six-month secured overnight financing rate,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: which is the global short-term rate benchmark in US dollars,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: is assumed to be within 3% to 4% in 2026 as well as in 2027.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: This reflects expectations that the US Fed

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: may maintain a relatively cautious stance

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: in terms of monetary policy.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Finally, our exports of goods will grow modestly,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: boosted by firm global demand for electronics and manufactures,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: but constrained by the slow global economy

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and increased global trade uncertainty.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Let me end with some remarks.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: First, inflation outlook remains elevated,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: requiring measured action to anchor inflation expectations

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and contain broadening price pressures.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: We have adequate external buffers

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: and a resilient, healthy banking system

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: to provide support to domestic economic activity.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Moving forward,

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: the BSP is prepared to take further monetary actions

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: if needed to ensure its primary mandate

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: of maintaining price stability

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: conducive to sustainable and durable growth.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: We end here, Madam Chair.

segments.speaker: BSP Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald R. Abenoja
segments.text: Again, thank you very much.

segments.speaker: Rep. Mikaela Angela B. Suansing
segments.text: Thank you very much to the BSP family.

segments.speaker: Rep. Mikaela Angela B. Suansing
segments.text: Thank you to Governor Eli Remolona Jr.

segments.speaker: Rep. Mikaela Angela B. Suansing
segments.text: and Deputy Governor Zeno Ronald,

segments.speaker: Rep. Mikaela Angela B. Suansing
segments.text: and Deputy Governor Abenoja.

segments.speaker: Rep. Mikaela Angela B. Suansing
segments.text: Thank you very much.

segments.speaker: Rep. Mikaela Angela B. Suansing
segments.text: Next, we move to the presentation

segments.speaker: Rep. Mikaela Angela B. Suansing
segments.text: of the Department of Economy, Planning and Development,

segments.speaker: Rep. Mikaela Angela B. Suansing
segments.text: or DEPDev,

segments.speaker: Rep. Mikaela Angela B. Suansing
segments.text: headed by Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan.

segments.speaker: Rep. Mikaela Angela B. Suansing
segments.text: Secretary Balisacan, kindly proceed po.

segments.speaker: Rep. Mikaela Angela B. Suansing
segments.text: Thank you very much.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Thank you, Speaker Di III,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Chairperson Swan Singh,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and distinguished members of the Committee on Appropriations

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: for this opportunity

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: to discuss the state of the Philippine economy

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and our economic directions moving forward.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: My task this morning

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: is to provide the economic development context

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: for the proposed 2027 National Budget,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: where the economy stands,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: why growth has slowed sharply in recent quarters,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and what directions must guide

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: our policies and investments moving forward.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The 2027 budget must help us

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: protect the gains already achieved,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: address critical implementations

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and structural bottlenecks,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and restore the economy to a faster,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: more durable, and inclusive growth path.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: I will cover three areas.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: First, our economic performance

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and recent developments.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Second, the emerging risk

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and persistent structural constraints.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: And third, our outlook and priorities

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: for recovering growth

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and laying the foundations for sustained development.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Let me begin with our economic performance.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Over the past several years,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: the Philippine economy achieved important gains

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: in growth, employment, and poverty reduction.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: More recent developments, however,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: show a sharp loss of momentum.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Taking the longer view,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: the Philippine economy has become stronger.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: From 2010 to 2025,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: real GDP grew by an average of 5.1% a year,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: faster than the 4.2% average

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: recorded during the preceding 15 years.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Following the pandemic,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: economic growth averaged 5.8%

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: from 2022 to 2025.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: However, momentum weakened sharply

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: beginning in the second half of 2025,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: with growth slowing further to 2.6%

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: in the first half of this year.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This sharp deceleration defines our immediate challenge

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: to recover growth without losing

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: the important development gains already achieved.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: That milestone is the Philippines' transition

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: to upper middle-income status

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: after nearly four decades

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: as a lower middle-income economy.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The country's gross national income per capita,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: or GNI,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: reached US$4,850 in 2025,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: surpassing the World Bank's threshold

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: As the chart on the right shows,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: the Philippines has also moved closer

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: to its Asian peers,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: although considerable income gaps remain.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Reaching upper middle-income status

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: is an important achievement,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: but it is or it is not an end in itself.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The greater challenge is to translate this progress

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: into better jobs, higher incomes,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and improved living standards for Filipinos.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: To do so, we must first understand the factors

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: behind the recent loss of economic momentum.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The sharp slowdown largely reflected

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: weaker domestic demand,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: as governance and corruption concerns

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and the Middle East conflict weighed

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: on consumer and business confidence.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Domestic demand grew by only 1.5%

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: in the first half of 2026,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: down from 5.7% in the same period last year.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Investment contracted by 6.5%,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: driven largely by the sharp decline

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: in public construction.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Household consumption growth also eased to 2.9%,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: amid elevated inflation and weaker confidence.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Exports provided some support,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: growing by 10%.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: On the production side, however,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: services remained the principal source of growth,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: while industry contracted and agriculture

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: made only a modest contribution.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The weakening of economic activity

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: has also begun to affect the labour market.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The post-pandemic expansion generated 4 million net jobs

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: between the first half of 2022 and the first half of 2026,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: demonstrating how economic growth can create opportunities

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and improve livelihoods.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: However, as growth slowed,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: total employment declined by 166,000 in the past year.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The unemployment rate also rose to 4.2% in June 2026,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: from 3.1% a year earlier.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: These recent developments underscore the urgency

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: of restoring economic momentum

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and generating more and better quality jobs.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The benefits of recent economic growth extended beyond employment,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: poverty declined substantially,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: regardless of the poverty threshold or norm used.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Based on the country's official poverty lines

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and the preliminary estimates for 2025,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: poverty incidence,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: or the proportion of the population deemed poor among Filipinos,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: fell from 18.1% in 2021 to 9.7% in 2025.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This means that 8.8 million Filipinos

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: were lifted out of poverty over this period.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: These gains reflect not only the recovery of incomes and employment,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: but also the sustained implementation of social protection programs.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: However, these hard-won gains remain vulnerable,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: particularly to high inflation,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: which disproportionately affects poor and low-income households.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: As Governor Remolona just mentioned,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: or discussed earlier,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: inflation rose sharply beginning in March,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: driven largely by the effects of the Middle East conflict

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: on global oil and commodity prices.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Headline inflation is slightly to 6.2% in July

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: from 6.4% in June,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: but it remains well above the government's target range.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: High inflation erodes household purchasing power,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: disproportionately affecting poor and low-income families.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The burden is even heavier

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: when food prices rise faster than non-food prices,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: as food accounts for a much larger share of total consumption spending

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: among low-income families than among high-income families.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: If inflation remains elevated,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: it could slow or even reverse

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: our recent gains in poverty reduction.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Protecting these gains while recovering economic growth

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: will require us to address both emerging risk

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and the economy's persistent structural constraints.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Beyond the immediate concerns of slower growth and elevated inflation,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: persistent structural constraints continue to limit

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: the economy's productive capacity and resilience.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Let me now turn to these constraints.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: A central structural challenge

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: is the economy's heavy reliance on household consumption

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: under the

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: side and services on the production side of the economy. Consumption remains the

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: principal driver of economic growth, while the contributions of fixed

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: investment exports, net of imports, have been relatively limited. Similarly,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: services account for most of the expansion, while agriculture and industry

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: have contributed much less. The experience of successful economies shows

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: that sustained progress requires mobilizing other sources of growth,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: notably investment, exports, agriculture, and industry. We must therefore broaden

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: the source of growth by strengthening investment and exports, while

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: revitalizing agriculture and industry. The urgency of this task is evident

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: from our performance relative to our ASEAN peers. As the charts show, the

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Philippines continues to trail several neighboring economies in both

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: fixed investment and exports, despite improvements in recent years.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Investment expands productive capacity, facilitates the adoption of new

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: technologies, and creates better jobs.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Exports enable domestic firms to reach larger markets, achieve economies of

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: scale, and become more competitive. Mobilizing greater investment and

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: improving export competitiveness will depend, critically, on high quality and

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: reliable infrastructure. The government has substantially increased

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: infrastructure spending in recent years. Yet, this higher level of expenditure has

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: not translated for the better. The government has substantially increased infrastructure spending in recent years. Yet, this higher level of expenditure has not translated

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: fully into stronger infrastructure competitiveness and the Philippines continues to trail several ASEAN peers.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: fully into stronger infrastructure competitiveness and the Philippines continues to trail several ASEAN peers.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This gap shows that the level of spending alone is not enough. We must also

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: improve project selection, appraisal, procurement, implementation, and

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: maintenance to ensure that public resources deliver high-quality

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: infrastructure on time and at reasonable cost.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Closing our infrastructure gaps will reduce production and logistic costs, connect people and markets, crowd in private investment, and strengthen the country's competitiveness.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Beyond physical infrastructure, faster growth also requires greater innovation and stronger productivity.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The Philippines has made encouraging progress in innovation, as reflected in its improved ranking in the Global Innovation Index.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: However, these gains have yet to translate into stronger overall productivity, that is, how efficiently the economy combines its workers, capital, technology, and other resources to produce goods and services.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: As the chart on the right shows,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: our productivity performance remains weak relative to several of our regional peers.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Innovation contributes to development only when new knowledge and technologies are widely adapted by firms, farms, and workers,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and translated into more efficient production, better products, and higher value activities.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: We must therefore strengthen the links among research, skills development, technology adoption,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: commercialization, and production.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The weaknesses we have discussed do not arise from a single source.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: They reflect persistent and interconnected constraints across markets and institutions.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: These include infrastructure and human capital gaps, regulatory and administrative burdens, limited access to finance and technology,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: weak competition in key sectors, and continuing governance concerns.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Together, these constraints raise the cost of doing business, discourage investment and innovation,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and limit the ability of firms and workers to move into more productive and higher-value activities.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Addressing them requires coordinated action across government in close partnership with Congress, the private sector, and other stakeholders.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Having identified these challenges,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: I now turn to our growth targets and the priorities for moving the economy forward.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Our directions remain anchored in the Philippine Development Plan.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Over the Administration's final two years, the emphasis is on accelerating execution,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: resolving implementation bottlenecks, and translating reforms into concrete results.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Given the sharp slowdown in recent years,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: economic growth is projected at 3.5 to 4.5 percent in 2025.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: With faster implementation of public programs and infrastructure projects,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: improved domestic supply conditions,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and restored consumer and investor confidence,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: growth is expected to recover to 5 to 6 percent in the next two years.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Inflation is expected to recover to 5 to 6 percent in the next two years.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Inflation is expected to remain elevated in 2026, as shown earlier by BSP,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: eased to 4 to 5 percent in 2027,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and returned to the government's targets of 2 to 4 percent target range by 2028.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Meanwhile, employment conditions are expected to improve as economic growth recovers,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: keeping unemployment within the government's target range.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Achieving these outcomes will require disciplined and coordinated execution across government,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: along with the timely implementation of reforms that encourage private investment

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and expand the economy's productive capacity.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: These targets are attainable,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: but they remain subject to significant domestic and external risk.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Achieving our growth, inflation, and employment targets

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: will require us to manage significant domestic and external risk.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Foremost among the domestic risks are further delays in the execution of public investments,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: resulting in continued underspending,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: as well as continuing governance concerns

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: that could further weaken consumer and investor confidence.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Severe weather disturbances could also constrain food production

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and intensify inflationary pressures.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Externally, the prolonged Middle East conflict

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: could keep global oil and commodity prices elevated,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: while geopolitical and trade tensions may weaken global demand

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and disrupt supply chains.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: These risks reinforce the need for timely and coordinated policies and execution

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: that address immediate pressures while strengthening the economy's productive capacity.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: In the near term,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: our priorities are to protect vulnerable households,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: accelerate public investments,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and restore confidence.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: First, we will caution poor and low-income families

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: from elevated food prices and supply disruptions

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: through targeted and timely assistance,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: while strengthening domestic food supply and maintaining adequate buffers.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Second, implementing agencies will accelerate high-impact infrastructure projects

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: through catch-up plans with clear milestones and accountability measures.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This is essential to reverse underspending

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and restore public investment as a driver of growth.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Third, we need to address governance and corruption concerns

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: by strengthening transparency and accountability,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: improving monitoring,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and ensuring the efficient use of public resources.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: These measures are critical to rebuilding consumer,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: business, and investor confidence.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Alongside these measures,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: our immediate interventions,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: we must sustain investments that expand the economy's productive capacity

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: over the short to medium term.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Over the short to medium term,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: limited public resources must be directed toward high-impact,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: implementation-ready investments.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Priorities include addressing learning poverty and classroom shortages,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: equipping workers with future-ready skills,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: strengthening primary health care,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: particularly in underserved areas,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: raising farm productivity through climate-resilient technologies

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and better post-harvest infrastructure,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and accelerating transport, logistics, energy,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and digital infrastructure

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: through the Build Better More program and public-private partnerships.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: These investments must be pursued

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: while safeguarding fiscal sustainability.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: This requires stronger coordination of planning,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: investment programming,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: budgeting, and execution of infrastructure and social programs,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: improved spending efficiency,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: modernized tax and customs administration,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and revenue measures that do not erode the government's fiscal position.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Beyond addressing immediate challenges,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: sustained and structural reforms will be needed to raise productivity,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: strengthen competitiveness,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and expand the economy's long-term growth potential.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Key priorities include ensuring more reliable and affordable energy

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: by expanding renewable generation,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: modernizing the power grid,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: streamlining net metering and permitting processes,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and strengthening competition in the electricity market.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Domestic production

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and external competitiveness must likewise be strengthened

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: by moving into higher value segments of global value chains,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: fostering stronger linkages between multinational and domestic firms,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: sustaining the country's advantage in high-value services,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and expanding market access for Philippine exports.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Deeper financial and capital markets will also be essential

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: to mobilize long-term financing for infrastructure

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: and productive enterprises.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Legislation will be indispensable to advancing this reform agenda.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: The priority measures span four broad areas.

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan
segments.text: Governance and anti-corruption reforms include measures on political dynasties,

segments.speaker: DEPDev Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan

segments.text: The honorable speaker, Bodjie Dy III,

segments.text: Chair Mika Suansing,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: on the national government's fiscal position.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Our fiscal position today has been shaped by key economic developments,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: from the circumstances this administration inherited

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: to the global conditions that have influenced our fiscal path since then.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Allow me to discuss briefly,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: to provide context to where we are today

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: and where we are headed.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: When the Marcos Jr. administration assumed office in 2022,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: it inherited a massive 12.79 trillion debt,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: the bulk of which was incurred from pandemic spending.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: So when the economy began to recover,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: the challenge before the administration was clear.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: To rebuild fiscal space,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: the government began to invest in the economy

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: while continuing to support economic recovery

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: and investing in the country's long-term growth.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: As a response,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: we crafted the country's medium-term fiscal framework in 2022.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: The government's blueprint for gradually reducing our deficit and debt

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: while creating more jobs,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: increasing people's incomes,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: and reducing poverty.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: It set us on a path of gradual and sustained fiscal consolidation

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: to restore fiscal space

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: while continuing to invest in the foundations of growth.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: But our recovery has not happened in an easy environment.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Over the years,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: external pressures and global uncertainties

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: have disrupted supply chains and pushed inflation up,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: affecting the pace of growth.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: In this context,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: we had to recalibrate our growth and fiscal targets

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: to keep them realistic and responsive

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: to evolving economic conditions.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: But the direction of our fiscal policy

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: has remained consistent.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: The administration has remained committed

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: to the path of fiscal consolidation

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: with the goal of bringing down

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: the deficit to GDP ratio

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: from 5.4% this year

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: to just 3.5% by 2030

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: while supporting growth.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: To stay the course amid growing political tensions

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: and the need to fund the government's priority programs

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: without relying on new taxes,

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: we strengthened revenues.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: Total revenues grew double digits

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: at an annual average of 10.5%

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: over the last four years.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: by an average of 10.47%

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: over the same period.

segments.text: And finally,

segments.text: for the first time in history,

segments.text: the BIR surpassed 3 trillion pesos

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: in tax collections.

segments.speaker: DOF Secretary Frederick D. Go
segments.text: And we continue to stay the course
